newsitem.title: USA: Dow sets another record, bonds rise, dollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dow sets another record, bonds rise, dollar mixed.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average set another record and bond prices rose Thursday, rebounding after investors shrugged off a rise in consumer prices last month. The dollar ended mixed.
Coffee prices soared to 20-year highs on frantic buying by speculators and roasters worried about small stockpiles and worries over the current crop.
The 30-share Dow jumped 47.39 points to 7,333.55 -- its first close above 7,300 and its 19th record so far this year -- as it eclipsed the old mark of 7,292.75 set on Monday.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,280 to 1,165 on moderate volume of 458 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks also set a record, rising 5.84 points to 841.88.

Blue-chip stocks had been stuck in a narrow range most of the session as some investors elected to wait ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting on interest rates on Tuesday. The central bank raised short-term rates in March, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to ward off inflation.
Conflicting economic news has sent mixed signals as to whether the Fed would raise interest rates next week.

"We see a 50-50 chance that the Fed may raise rates just to continue with their pre-emptive strike but the inflation numbers have looked pretty good this week," said Elaine Garzarelli, who remains bullish with a year-end target of 7,600 for the Dow.

Financial markets fell initially after the government reported said the core rate of inflation, excluding volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3 percent as measured by the Consumer Price Index. The gain exceeded Wall Street forecasts.

Overall the CPI rose 0.1 percent last month, matching the 0.1 percent rise in March. Economists had predicted the overall index would rise by 0.1 percent, and they expected the core rate to climb by just 0.2 percent.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury rose 7/32, or $2.19 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.87 percent from 6.88 percent on Wednesday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.

The dollar plunged to 114.70 yen, its lowest level since Dec. 27, 1996, in Europe on expectations that Japan will raise interest rates. In late New York trading, the dollar settled at 115.97 yen, down from 117.23 yen late Wednesday.
But the dollar rose to 1.6980 German marks from 1.6947 amid concern that the German government may revalue some of its gold to help shrink the country's yawning budget deficit.
Gold prices edged higher as traders puzzled over German announcements about the fate of gold now held in the vaults of the Bundesbank.
Gold for June delivery at the COMEX in New York closed 20 cents an ounce higher at $348.40 after falling more than $2 on Wednesday when it appeared Germany might sell gold.

At the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange in New York, coffee for May delivery closed at 277.05 cents a pound, up 15.55 cents, after trading as high as 279 cents -- the highest price for a coffee futures contract on the exchange since June 1977.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybean prices fell after a weekly report showing lower-than-expected exports. Soybeans for May delivery closed down 7 cents a bushel at $8.62.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index fell 5.7 points to 4,681.2. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average lost 153.41 points to close at 20,056.31.
